summary.name: Crisp
summary.one_liner: Crisp is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app for external monitor control, covering HiDPI scaling, DDC brightness, presets, arrangement, and a command line tool.
use_cases: Fix blurry or tiny text on an external monitor
Control external monitor brightness with keyboard keys
Save and apply display setups with presets
Switch a monitor's input from the Mac
Automate day and night display setups with Shortcuts
Script display settings from the terminal
summary.what_it_does: Crisp is a macOS menu bar panel for managing external monitors. It provides HiDPI (Retina-style) scaled resolutions and fine-grained scaling on external displays, plus hardware DDC brightness with software fallback and brightness keys. Presets save resolution, brightness, arrangement, image adjustment, HDR and which displays are active, and can be applied from the menu or on a schedule via Shortcuts. A command line tool, crispctl, ships inside the app for controlling brightness, HDR, presets, monitor input and display connection from scripts.
notable: Open source under the MIT license, listed in awesome-mac
Extra Brightness unlocks HDR brightness reserve on XDR MacBooks and HDR monitors
crispctl command line tool and Apple Shortcuts actions
Virtual HiDPI displays for streaming, sidecar, or headless Macs
caveats: Disconnecting displays from the menu is Apple Silicon only
Developer signing and notarization is funded by optional donations ($99/year Apple Developer membership)
